newsitem.title: UK: Benazir Bhutto may seek asylum in Britain - paper.
newsitem.headline: Benazir Bhutto may seek asylum in Britain - paper.

text.p: Former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto may seek asylum in Britain, a British newspaper said.
The Sunday Times said a deal was being secretly considered by the government in Pakistan to avoid civil unrest that could result from putting her on trial.
The newspaper quoted senior Pakistani government sources as saying the deal would be put to Bhutto if she loses Monday's elections as expected.
It said corruption charges against Bhutto and her husband Asif Ali Zardari would be dropped in exchange for her leaving the country. The alternative would be a politically sensistive trial.

President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto from the premiership in November, a decision endorsed this week by Pakistan's Supreme Court which found evidence against her of corruption, nepotism and misrule.

In a BBC television programme broadcast on Saturday, Zardari, who is in jail awaiting trial on charges of conspiracy to murder Bhutto's brother, accused Leghari of making corruption allegations against him in order to get at his wife.
Bhutto dismissed allegations of corruption against herself and her husband as "lies".
Pakistanis vote on Monday in new national assembly elections which polls indicate Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party is set to lose.
The Sunday Times said that if she accepted the asylum plan Bhutto would have to promise to quit politics.
The deal would provide a neat solution for the Pakistani government, which fears that a high-profile trial could inflame passions and lead to widespread unrest, the paper said.

The British Home Office said only that for Bhutto to be granted asylum in Britain she would have to be persecuted in her own country either because of her religious beliefs, ethnicity or political views.
